LCM Freestyle Progression Model

Probabilistic four-year forecasts for national-level age-group swimmers, conditional on continuing to train and compete. The model estimates distributions, not physiological ceilings or guarantees.

Swimmer inputs

Enter at least two dated long-course personal bests. PB dates matter: performances achieved at different ages are not treated as simultaneous.

Current estimated profile

Reference positions are within the model's selected national/elite competitive reference sample; they are not literal global percentiles. Higher positions correspond to faster swimming.

100m freestyle

Default view: Projected PB by date. Each simulated path carries forward the best time achieved to date, so a PB cannot become slower. A plateau appears as a flat median while faster-tail outcomes may continue to improve.
Median projected PBCentral 60% and 80% PB bandsSupplied dated PB

The vertical scale is swimming time: faster times appear higher. Projected PB is the running best of each coherent simulated path; the underlying period-performance model remains available from the forecast-view selector.

Projected PB distribution

Projected-PB percentile: higher percentiles mean faster swimming. P90 is the fast/optimistic end and P10 the slower/conservative end. Each simulated path uses the running best time achieved by that date, so no projected PB percentile can become slower over time. For a supplied event, the current PB is treated as known; uncertainty concerns when and by how much it may be improved.

The cumulative-PB display is derived from the same calibrated period-performance paths used in v4.4. The period/season view is retained for diagnosing plateaus and temporary regression.

Target and benchmark probabilities

These are cumulative probabilities of having achieved the stated time by each forecast date on the model's six-month grid. Probabilities below 10% are deliberately rounded and accompanied by an approximate finite-data model-risk range.

No target or benchmark available for this event.

The displayed model-risk range is not a formal confidence interval. It reflects finite transition-pool support and is intended to prevent false precision for rare outcomes. World/NZ records and Olympic/World Championship standards are external benchmarks. To keep the display compact, only A qualification standards are shown; B standards remain embedded in the model data.

Methodology, assumptions and validation

Methodology

Reference data and target populationThe model is designed for national-level and stronger age-group swimmers. Core transition estimates are derived principally from swimmer-linked Dutch national junior/senior race histories, with Australian elite-age-group evidence used to calibrate the upper tail and New Zealand age-group data used as an external geographic check.
Dated PBs and current stateEach supplied PB is used at its actual age/date rather than treated as simultaneous. Older PBs help estimate the swimmer's latent current period-performance state, but the supplied PB itself remains the known cumulative best at the reference date. If one or two events are missing, validated regularised multivariate models estimate the current event level with additional uncertainty.
Forecast distributionFuture period/season performance is modelled empirically by sex, event, age and current performance level. Annual marginals are directly calibrated; half-year marginals use direct six-month evidence where it passed training-only calibration gates and otherwise shrink toward annual interpolation. The default projected-PB distribution is then derived path-by-path as the running minimum (best time) of the known/current best and future simulated period performances.
Joint trajectories and probabilitiesMonte Carlo paths preserve observed dependence across freestyle distances and successive horizons. Cumulative PB paths therefore cannot worsen, although the underlying period-performance paths can plateau or regress. Target/benchmark probabilities use those cumulative paths and are conditional on remaining an active competitive swimmer.
SCM evidenceShort-course observations are retained as an auxiliary course-aware evidence stream rather than assumed identical to LCM. Headline outcome validation remains against genuine future LCM performances; proposed SCM-origin long-horizon changes that did not generalise externally were rejected.
Elite-tail treatmentAustralian All-Time Age Top-10 histories provide a smooth, capped upper-tail calibration adjustment near elite age-group territory. They are not treated as an ordinary population sample and do not define the denominator for international-success probabilities.

Key assumptions

  • Forecasts are conditional on the swimmer continuing to train and compete; dropout, injury and retention are not modelled.
  • The model estimates historical conditional distributions, not physiological ceilings, causal effects of training, or guaranteed outcomes.
  • The displayed model-reference position is relative to the selected national/elite reference sample and is not a literal global percentile.
  • Future coaching, training load, maturation timing, illness and life circumstances are latent sources of outcome uncertainty rather than explicit user inputs.
  • Four-year event-specific evidence remains materially thinner than one- and two-year evidence, particularly for 400m freestyle.
  • Rare World/Olympic-level probabilities have limited empirical resolution; displayed model-risk ranges are intended to avoid false percentage-point precision.
  • Records and qualifying standards are external, time-varying benchmarks and can be updated without retraining the progression model.
  • The v4.5 cumulative-PB layer is a coherent transformation of the validated period-performance trajectories. The historical validation gates shown below apply principally to the underlying period-performance marginals; cumulative-PB calibration should be separately re-tested as more longitudinal PB-history data become available.

Data and research sources

  • KNZB LiveTiming and public Dutch competition results - principal swimmer-linked longitudinal microdata.
  • Swimming Australia rankings and records - All-Time Age Top-10 elite-tail trajectories.
  • Swimming New Zealand / SwimInfo - external national-age-group evidence and NZ record benchmarks.
  • Born et al., normative LCM swimming percentile research - external age/performance reference context.
  • World/Olympic qualification benchmarks and World Records are sourced separately from official governing-body publications; the current benchmark links are listed below.

Validation gates carried into this version

Each material modelling change was retained only after improving its specified held-out test. These are development diagnostics, not guarantees for an individual swimmer.

Benchmark provenance

    Benchmark data are stored separately from fitted progression parameters so future standards can be updated without retraining the model.

    Important limitations

    • The principal microdata remain dominated by Dutch national junior/senior meets, with Australian and New Zealand elite/national-age-group external evidence.
    • Australian all-time Age Top-10 histories improve elite-tail calibration, but that panel is selected on exceptional performance and repeat appearance.
    • Half-year calibration is empirical where supported, but +2.5/+3.5 year event cells are smaller than +0.5/+1.5 and some are deliberately shrunk toward annual interpolation.
    • Four-year validation remains sparse, especially for 400m freestyle.
    • Ages 10–11 have limited direct microdata support and rely heavily on the ≤13 fallback distribution.
    All calculations run locally in this browser. No swimmer inputs are transmitted or stored externally.
